correctness.rationale: The derived ideal is Kz, so D(z)=az. If a is nonzero a rank-one image is Kz, which makes the right-hand side of the derivation law zero and contradicts aB≠0. Write the remaining noncentral case as D(v)=ψ(v)(u+cz). Applying the law with one argument in ker ψ forces both B(u,−) and B(−,u) to be multiples of ψ, and with both arguments outside that kernel their coefficients sum to zero. Nondegeneracy makes the first coefficient nonzero. This yields precisely the stated normal form on W_B, including the converse and the uniqueness for fixed projective representatives. Squaring gives D²=tB(u,u)D. The central type contributes qⁿ−1, each line in W_B contributes q(q−1), and in characteristic two the square root of B(u,u) on W_B is a linear functional over the finite field. If it is nonzero exactly q^(r−1) lines lie outside its kernel, each giving q maps per prescribed nonzero scalar. In odd characteristic 2B(u,u)=0 on W_B, so that exceptional case cannot occur. Independent direct basis-pair tests using normalized rank-one factors corroborated, for example, totals 75 and idempotent counts 16 versus 0 for I₂ and the alternating plane over F₄. Over F₄ with B=diag(1, [[1,1],[0,1]]), r=1, the observed counts by scalar were 63,4,4,4, testing a proper symmetrization radical. These are bounded reproductions; the tensor-factor argument supplies the universal proof. The frozen verification file and checker were inspected, not executed.
